articles.originalTitle: Chinese President Xi Jinping meets Mexican president in Shenzhen
articles.originalFullText:
Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Tuesday that advancing China-Mexico relations to new heights, across broader areas and in greater depth is of great significance to implementing their respective national development strategies and supporting the Global South in seeking strength through unity.

Xi made the remarks while meeting with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting from November 18 to 19.

China is ready to work with Mexico to steer bilateral relations toward high-quality development, promote the building of an Asia Pacific that is prosperous, stable, open, interconnected, universally beneficial, inclusive, united and mutually supportive, as well as a more just and equitable global governance system, and contribute to world peace and common development, Xi added.

Xi called on China and Mexico to deepen political mutual trust, strengthen exchanges and cooperation at all levels, stay committed to mutual benefit and win-win results, strengthen strategic alignment, and deepen cooperation on infrastructure, science and technology, clean energy, culture and tourism.

He stressed the need for both sides to uphold fairness and justice, boost multilateral cooperation, enhance coordination at multilateral platforms such as the United Nations, and safeguard the basic norms governing international relations.

Xi also called for deepening cooperation between China and Latin American and Caribbean (LAC) countries by advancing the five programs for the China-LAC community with a shared future.

Noting that Mexico and China enjoy deep-rooted friendship, share similar development philosophies and have witnessed fruitful cooperation across various fields, Sheinbaum said Mexico is ready to expand cooperation with China in areas such as trade, investment, science and technology, manufacturing and artificial intelligence, while promoting exchanges in health, education, culture and tourism.

She said China, as this year's APEC host, has played an important role in advancing Asia-Pacific cooperation, expressing confidence that the upcoming APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting would be a complete success and lay a solid foundation for future regional cooperation.

Mexico stands ready to work with China to strengthen multilateral coordination, uphold multilateralism and safeguard the common interests of the Global South, said Sheinbaum.

Председатель КНР Си Цзиньпин заявил во вторник, что продвижение китайско-мексиканских отношений на новые высоты, в более широких областях и в большей глубине имеет большое значение для реализации их соответствующих национальных стратегий развития и поддержки глобального Юга в поиске силы через единство.

Си Цзиньпин выступил с речью во время встречи с президентом Мексики Клаудией Шейнбаум Пардо, которая находится в Шэньчжэне для участия в 33-й встрече лидеров экономик Азиатско-Тихоокеанского экономического сотрудничества (АТЭС) с 18 по 19 ноября.

Китай готов работать с Мексикой, чтобы направить двусторонние отношения к высококачественному развитию, содействовать строительству Азиатско-Тихоокеанского региона, который является процветающим, стабильным, открытым, взаимосвязанным, универсально выгодным, инклюзивным, объединенным и взаимоподдерживающим, а также более справедливой и справедливой глобальной системой управления и вносит вклад в мир во всем мире и общее развитие.

Си Цзиньпин призвал Китай и Мексику углублять политическое взаимное доверие, укреплять обмены и сотрудничество на всех уровнях, оставаться приверженными взаимной выгоде и взаимовыгодным результатам, укреплять стратегическое выравнивание и углублять сотрудничество в области инфраструктуры, науки и техники, чистой энергии, культуры и туризма.

Он подчеркнул необходимость того, чтобы обе стороны поддерживали справедливость и справедливость, укрепляли многостороннее сотрудничество, укрепляли координацию на многосторонних платформах, таких как Организация Объединенных Наций, и защищали основные нормы, регулирующие международные отношения.

Си Цзиньпин также призвал к углублению сотрудничества между Китаем и странами Латинской Америки и Карибского бассейна путем продвижения пяти программ для сообщества Китай-ЛАК с общим будущим.

Отметив, что Мексика и Китай пользуются глубоко укоренившейся дружбой, разделяют схожие философии развития и стали свидетелями плодотворного сотрудничества в различных областях, Шейнбаум сказал, что Мексика готова расширить сотрудничество с Китаем в таких областях, как торговля, инвестиции, наука и техника, производство и искусственный интеллект, одновременно способствуя обмену в области здравоохранения, образования, культуры и туризма.

Китай, как принимающая сторона АТЭС в этом году, сыграл важную роль в развитии азиатско-тихоокеанского сотрудничества, выразив уверенность в том, что будущие экономические лидеры АТЭС будут участвовать в этом процессе. Встреча будет иметь полный успех и заложит прочную основу для будущего регионального сотрудничества.

Мексика готова работать с Китаем для укрепления многосторонней координации, поддержки многосторонности и защиты общих интересов Глобального Юга, - сказал Шейнбаум.

articles.originalFullText:
China remains a key market for US companies, not only for its market size, manufacturing strength and supply chains, but also for its growing innovation across various sectors, Michael Hart, president of AmCham China told CGTN Digital reporter Shen Shiwei in an interview.

Why does China continue to be an important and critical market for US businesses? Hart explained that during his knock door visits to Washington DC, the chamber engages with US lawmakers, think tanks and business representatives to explain the value of maintaining a presence in China. He highlighted innovation in sectors such as pharmaceuticals as another key reason for US companies to remain in China, adding that the chamber will continue to share this message with policymakers and the business community in the US.

articles.originalTitle: Xi urges faster building of fair, efficient socialist judicial system
articles.originalText: Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged efforts to speed up the building of a fair, efficient and authoritative socialist judicial system and safeguard high-quality development and high-level security with high-quality judicial services.
articles.originalFullText:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged efforts to speed up the building of a fair, efficient and authoritative socialist judicial system and safeguard high-quality development and high-level security with high-quality judicial services.

Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction on the work related to the people's courts.

People's courts at all levels have provided a strong judicial guarantee for reform, development and stability since the 18th National Congress of the CPC in 2012, Xi said.

He called for efforts to deepen the reform of the judicial system and regulate the exercise of judicial power.

In the process, Xi stressed the need to fully implement the thought on socialist rule of law with Chinese characteristics for the new era, and to adhere to the leadership of the CPC, a people-centered approach, the path of socialist rule of law with Chinese characteristics, and the independent and impartial exercise of adjudicatory power in accordance with the law.

Efforts should be made to build strong and capable teams of loyal, upright and responsible personnel, Xi said, urging new and greater contributions to advancing the Peaceful China Initiative and the rule of law to a higher level, and to advancing Chinese modernization.

Xi's instruction was conveyed at a national conference on the work of the people's courts held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday.

Chen Wenqing, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and head of the Commission for Political and Legal Affairs of the CPC Central Committee, attended and addressed the event.

Chen said each stage of judicial services, from case filing and trials to enforcement and litigation-related petitions, should follow the principle of serving the people to safeguard fairness and justice.

The conference was presided over by Zhang Jun, president of the Supreme People's Court.

Председатель КНР Си Цзиньпин призвал ускорить создание справедливой, эффективной и авторитетной социалистической судебной системы и обеспечить качественное развитие и безопасность на высоком уровне с помощью высококачественных судебных услуг.

Си Цзиньпин, также генеральный секретарь Центрального комитета Коммунистической партии Китая (КПК) и председатель Центральной военной комиссии, сделал эти замечания в недавнем поручении о работе, связанной с народными судами.

Народные суды на всех уровнях обеспечили сильную судебную гарантию для реформ, развития и стабильности с 18-го Национального конгресса КПК в 2012 году.

Он призвал прилагать усилия для углубления реформы судебной системы и регулирования осуществления судебной власти.

В процессе Си Цзиньпин подчеркнул необходимость в полной мере реализовать мысль о социалистическом верховенстве права с китайской спецификой для новой эпохи и придерживаться руководства КПК, ориентированного на людей подхода, пути социалистического верховенства права с китайской спецификой и независимого и беспристрастного осуществления судебной власти в соответствии с законом.

Необходимо приложить усилия для создания сильных и способных команд преданного, честного и ответственного персонала, - сказал Си Цзиньпин, призвав внести новый и больший вклад в продвижение Инициативы мирного Китая и верховенства закона на более высокий уровень и в продвижение китайской модернизации.

Инструкция Си была передана на национальной конференции по работе народных судов, состоявшейся в Пекине в понедельник и вторник.

Чэнь Вэньцин, член Политбюро ЦК КПК и глава Комиссии по политико-правовым вопросам ЦК КПК, присутствовал и выступил на мероприятии.

Чэнь сказал, что каждый этап судебных услуг, от подачи дел и судебных процессов до исполнения и судебных петиций, связанных с судебными разбирательствами, должен следовать принципу служения народу для обеспечения справедливости и справедливости.

Конференция проходила под председательством Чжан Цзюня, председателя Верховного народного суда.

articles.originalTitle: Condominium flippers face 50% tax under plan to curb speculation
articles.originalText: The government and ruling coalition are considering imposing a 50-percent tax on profits gained from resales of newly built condominiums within a year of purchase to curb speculation and soaring prices in urban areas. The proposed rate is aimed at people who buy new condominiums not for living purposes but to make quick profits through resales. Individuals currently pay combined income and residential taxes of about 40 percent on profits from property held for five years or less, and about 20 percent after five years. The proposal would raise the rate by about 10 percentage points for qualifying condominium sales.
articles.title: Кондоминиуму грозит 50% налог в рамках плана по сдерживанию спекуляций
articles.text: Правительство и правящая коалиция рассматривают возможность введения 50-процентного налога на прибыль, полученную от перепродажи недавно построенных кондоминиумов в течение года после покупки, чтобы обуздать спекуляции и взлет цен в городских районах. Предлагаемая ставка предназначена для людей, которые покупают новые кондоминиумы не для проживания, а для получения быстрой прибыли путем перепродажи. Физические лица в настоящее время платят совокупный доход и налоги на жилье около 40 процентов от прибыли от имущества, удерживаемого в течение пяти лет или менее, и около 20 процентов после пяти лет. Предложение повысит ставку примерно на 10 процентных пунктов для квалификационных продаж кондоминиумов.

'Quite a stupid thing': Germany, UK reject US criticism of Ukraine deep strikes

Germany and Britain on Tuesday rejected Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby's criticism that Ukraine's deep strikes on Russian oil infrastructure and commercial warehouses were ineffective and risked hardening Russian resolve.

The clash laid bare a widening rift between Washington and its European allies over how Ukraine should wage the war, even as Europe and Canada have stepped in to fund arms supplies after the US stopped doing so under President Donald Trump.

Asked whether he shared Colby's position, German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius said "criticising strikes like that in Russia to destroy strategic military and military-used targets" was "quite a stupid thing".

"Instead of criticising that, we should rather criticize and talk about the terroristic strikes every night and every day on... energy, water, and heating infrastructure in Ukraine. This is kind of terrorism," Pistorius said.

British Defence Minister Wes Streeting took the same line, saying those strikes "helped to degrade (Russian President Vladimir) Putin's war machine, buying time and saving lives".

Speaking at NATO's Brussels headquarters, Colby likened Ukraine's deep strike campaign to a spectacle.

Zelensky on bridge strike: 'Russia chooses further escalation'

President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Tuesday that the attack on the Russian-built bridge linking Crimea to Russia was another strike on a major Russian target after enduring numerous attacks on bridges, infrastructure and cities.

"We have long been telling Russia: Enough of striking bridges, cities and villages, energy infrastructure, railways and grain ships. Enough of war. But every time Russia chooses further escalation," Zelenskiy said in his nightly video address.

"So Ukrainian missiles and Ukrainian drones have once again reached a key Russian military artery in the south. This is a result of the Security Service of Ukraine, all our Defence Forces of Ukraine..."

Moldova temporarily closes airspace after drone detected near Chisinau

Moldova temporarily shut the country's airspace for security reasons on Tuesday afternoon after a Shahed-type drone was detected heading towards the capital, Chisinau, the authorities said.

The eastern European country bordering Ukraine has reported several fallen drones on its territory since the beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

"For security reasons, the authorities have closed down the entire airspace of the Republic of Moldova," the defence ministry said in a statement.

The authorities urged Moldovans not to approach suspicious flying objects and not to touch drone debris, as this could contain "explosive elements".

In a statement on social media, the police said it had received several calls from residents of Chisinau and the surrounding area reporting the sound of explosions.

Moldovan President Maia Sandu criticised what she called "the boundless cynicism of Moscow's leaders" and vowed to continue supporting Kyiv.

European leaders should talk to Putin directly, Finnish president says

Finland's President Alexander Stubb urged European leaders to speak directly with Russian President Vladimir Putin, in an interview with the Financial Times on Tuesday.

Outsourcing talks with Russia to the US was not a responsible course of action, according to Stubb's comments to the business paper.

Stubb and Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store held a "frank and substantive" phone call in October with Putin about efforts to end the war in Ukraine.

Europe has been readying itself to take direct part in talks on ending Moscow's war after US envoys said last week that the Kremlin had agreed to let it join.

EU leaders last week agreed that France, along with Britain, Germany, Italy, Poland and the EU institutions should represent Europe.

Russian drone flew over Moldovan capital, president says

Moldovan President Maia Sandu said on Tuesday that a Russian drone flew over the capital Chisinau and pledged to press for further sanctions on Moscow.

"This evening several Russian drones violated our airspace, one of them over Chisinau, alarming residents," Sandu wrote on X.

"Russia's war threatens all of Europe. Moldova stands for peace. We'll keep pushing for sanctions on Moscow, standing with Ukraine and building our defence with partners.

Top US official criticises Ukraine's 'deep strikes' against Russia, citing escalation risk

US Defense Under Secretary Elbridge Colby criticised Ukraine's "deep strikes" against Russia Tuesday, saying they "have not been effective in driving an end to the war" or in blunting Russia's advances.

"Such strikes, especially those that target civilian infrastructure such as Wildberries, have actually probably hardened the Russian public's resolve and the Kremlin's own willingness to escalate," Colby told a gathering of Ukraine's backers at NATO headquarters in Brussels, referring to a Russian e-commerce giant targeted by Kyiv.

French troops in Ukraine a 'direct participation' in conflict, Russia says

Russia said Tuesday it was aware of French troops having been sent to Ukraine, calling it "direct participation" in the war and saying a message had been issued to Paris.

"Not only French ones, we know this. We have conveyed our concern... this is no longer support for Ukraine, but direct participation in the war," Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told reporters.

His remarks come a day after a source told AFP and other media that French soldiers had been operating in Ukraine for several months to train Ukrainian personnel and help maintain equipment.

A source told AFP earlier the mission of a small contingent of French troops excludes any combat role.

France on Tuesday rejected as "absurd" a claim by the Russian foreign minister that a contingent of French troops deployed in Ukraine were directly involved in fighting against Moscow.

There is a "very limited" deployment of French troops in Ukraine for training and equipment maintenance, deputy defence minister Alice Rufo told parliament. But "there is the absence of any intention to fight, contrary to what the Russian foreign minister (Sergei Lavrov) said this morning, which is absurd."

Ukraine offers humanitarian mission for 10 settlements, Zelensky says

Ukraine has offered to carry out a humanitarian mission similar to the one in Russia-occupied Oleshky for 10 settlements in the southern Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said.

"Our team will discuss this with the American mediators," he said on X.

Ukraine struck Russia's Crimean bridge for the second night in a row on Tuesday, shutting it down, while Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv -- the latest wave of attacks that come ahead of a historic meeting of the Chinese, US and Russian leaders.

Finland's president says clear timeline, agenda important for Russia-Ukraine negotiations

Finland's President Alexander Stubb said on Tuesday it was important to get a clear timetable and agenda for the negotiations between Russia and Ukraine.

Russia will continue fuel imports, Kremlin says

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak has told a meeting of government representatives, oil producers and other officials to continue work to secure fuel imports, the Kremlin announced in a statement.

Russia, normally one of the world's largest fuel exporters, had to start importing gasoline and other oil products last summer following a spate of Ukrainian drone attacks on its oil refineries.

Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge in Crimea with drones and missiles

Ukrainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, calling it an “unprecedented” operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day. Meanwhile, Russia struck two major bridges in Kyiv.

Estonia to send 70 locomotives to Ukraine

Estonia is planning to send more than 70 locomotives to Ukraine to help maintain its railway network amid intensifying Russian attacks, Kyiv Independent reported, citing Estonia’s Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna.

The first deliveries could arrive before the end of this year, he said.

Ukraine says it has hit Salavat oil refinery in Russia's Bashkortostan

Ukraine's military said on Tuesday it had struck the Salavat oil refinery and petrochemical complex in Russia's Bashkortostan region.

In a post on Telegram, the General Staff said the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat plant was hit overnight, about 1,500 km (930 miles) from the Ukrainian border and that explosions were heard and a fire broke out at the site.

"Salavat is no ordinary plant. It is one of Russia's largest oil refining and petrochemical complexes, capable of processing about 10 million tonnes of oil a year," it said.

Hungary-Ukraine Railway traffic suspended after Russian drone attack

Hungary is suspending railway traffic to and from Ukraine on Tuesday and Wednesday after a Russian drone attack in western Ukraine, Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar wrote in a Facebook post on Tuesday.

Magyar said the decision was made after a Russian drone struck a location 300 meters from the railway station in the town of Mukachevo.

Crimea Bridge closed to road traffic after strikes cause partial collapse: Ukrainian military

The Ukrainian military has said that the Crimea Bridge is closed to road traffic after drone and missile strikes caused a road section of the bridge to collapse, falling into the water below.

Strikes also damaged a railway arch it added.

"For the occupiers, this is more than a symbolic blow. The bridge was the main artery carrying fuel, ammunition, equipment and personnel to the peninsula and on into southern Ukraine... The occupiers are left with fewer and fewer land routes to Crimea," it added.

- Russian President Vladimir Putin could meet North Korean leader Kim Jong-Un if he also attends this week's APEC summit in China, Interfax news agency quoted Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov as saying on Monday.

- Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky says intelligence shows that Russia is planning new strikes on Ukrainian targets Monday evening, overnight and Tuesday, according to a report by Reuters.

Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday arrived in China where he is expected to meet with his US and Chinese counterparts Donald Trump and Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the APEC summit, Russian state media reported. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

'Quite a stupid thing': Germany, UK reject US criticism of Ukraine deep strikes

Germany and Britain on Tuesday rejected Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby's criticism that Ukraine's deep strikes on Russian oil infrastructure and commercial warehouses were ineffective and risked hardening Russian resolve.

The clash laid bare a widening rift between Washington and its European allies over how Ukraine should wage the war, even as Europe and Canada have stepped in to fund arms supplies after the US stopped doing so under President Donald Trump.

Asked whether he shared Colby's position, German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius said "criticising strikes like that in Russia to destroy strategic military and military-used targets" was "quite a stupid thing".

"Instead of criticising that, we should rather criticize and talk about the terroristic strikes every night and every day on... energy, water, and heating infrastructure in Ukraine. This is kind of terrorism," Pistorius said.

British Defence Minister Wes Streeting took the same line, saying those strikes "helped to degrade (Russian President Vladimir) Putin's war machine, buying time and saving lives".

Speaking at NATO's Brussels headquarters, Colby likened Ukraine's deep strike campaign to a spectacle.

articles.title: Путин прибыл в Китай в преддверии трехстороннего саммита Трамп-Си
articles.text: Президент России Владимир Путин в среду прибыл в Китай, где, как ожидается, встретится со своими американскими и китайскими коллегами Дональдом Трампом и Си Цзиньпином в кулуарах саммита АТЭС, сообщают российские государственные СМИ. Российское государственное информационное агентство ТАСС сообщило, что самолет Путина приземлился в международном аэропорту Баоань в Шэньчжэне. Путин примет участие в саммите на этой неделе. Следите за нашим блогом, чтобы увидеть, как разворачивались события дня.

articles.text: Согласно новым правилам, у Министерства внутренних дел будет шесть месяцев, чтобы удалить человека, не сообщая им заранее.

articles.originalTitle: Hard bargain: Should Ukraine trade Donbas for NATO membership?
articles.originalText: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is asserting that the United States has asked him about a straight-up swap: Russia gets the Donbas and the rest of Ukraine gets NATO membership – a guarantee against Moscow later having a second go and annexing the entire country. Whether or not the offer is real, serious or either side would accept it is another matter. We ask if the talk of partition signals some kind of turning point in a nearly five-year war that's at a brutal stalemate.
articles.originalFullText:
President Volodymyr Zelensky asserting that the United States has asked him about a straight-up swap Russia gets the Donbas, the rest of Ukraine gets NATO membership, a guarantee against Moscow later having a second go and annexing the entire country. Whether or not the offer’s real, serious or that either side would accept it. We’ll ask if the talk of partition signals some kind of turning point in a nearly five-year war that's also a brutal stalemate.

The remarks came just days ahead of a three-way summit in Shenzhen, China that some have likened to Yalta, the 1945 carving up of Europe between the Soviets and Anglo-Americans. A fair comparison? From weekend border tensions between Russia and Estonia to EU leaders’ inability to agree on a single name to represent the bloc in Ukraine war talks, we’ll ask what this crucial week means for the future of the continent, where some of Ukraine's strongest backers may be on borrowed time. Enter French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen, the far-right leader whose 2017 campaign was financed by a Russian bank. She knows a majority of her compatriots support Ukraine, hence a courtesy call this Monday to its ambassador in Paris. But after she repeated that if elected, she'll pull the plug on financing for Kyiv.

Produced by Rebecca Gnignati, Elisa Amiri, Ilayda Habip.
articles.fullText:
Президент Владимир Зеленский утверждает, что Соединенные Штаты спросили его о прямом обмене Россией Донбасса, остальная часть Украины получает членство в НАТО, гарантию против того, чтобы Москва позже получила второй шанс и аннексировала всю страну. Будет ли предложение реальным, серьезным или любая из сторон примет его. Мы спросим, сигнализирует ли разговор о разделе о каком-то поворотном моменте в почти пятилетней войне, которая также является жестоким тупиком.

Замечания прозвучали всего за несколько дней до трехстороннего саммита в Шэньчжэне, Китай, который некоторые сравнивают с Ялтой, разделившей Европу в 1945 году между Советами и англо-американцами. Справедливое сравнение? От напряженности на границе между Россией и Эстонией до неспособности лидеров ЕС договориться о едином названии, чтобы представлять блок на переговорах по войне в Украине, мы спросим, что эта важная неделя означает для будущего континента, где некоторые из самых сильных сторонников Украины могут быть в заемное время. Войдите во французский президентский лидер Марин Ле Пен, крайне правый лидер, чья кампания 2017 года финансировалась российским банком. Она знает, что большинство ее соотечественников поддерживают Украину, поэтому в понедельник вежливо позвонит ее послу в Париже. Но после того, как она повторит, что в случае избрания, она отключит финансирование для Киева.

Продюсеры: Ребекка Гнигнати, Элиза Амири, Илайда Хабип.
articles.title: Сложная сделка: стоит ли Украине торговать Донбассом ради членства в НАТО?
articles.text: Президент Украины Владимир Зеленский утверждает, что Соединенные Штаты спросили его о прямом обмене: Россия получает Донбасс, а остальная часть Украины получает членство в НАТО - гарантия против того, чтобы Москва позже второй раз аннексировала всю страну. Является ли предложение реальным, серьезным или любая из сторон примет его, это другой вопрос. Мы спрашиваем, сигнализирует ли разговор о разделе какой-то поворотный момент в почти пятилетней войне, которая находится в жестоком тупике.

articles.originalTitle: Czech mass protests: Media is the first casualty 'when you want to attack democracy'
articles.originalText: As hundreds of thousands of people gather in Prague to protest the Czech government's proposal to replace public broadcasting licence fees with direct state funding, Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Bára Stárek, Executive Director of Díky, že můžem. Stárek warns that the proposed changes offer "no real safeguards" against political influence, pointing to developments in Slovakia and Hungary. She also drew a parallel with the Velvet Revolution of 1989, recalling that "we didn't have a free media and we only had a state media" under communist rule. "Media is the first (line of) attack when you want to attack democracy," she said.
articles.originalFullText:
Video contentVideo

As hundreds of thousands of people gather in Prague to protest the Czech government's proposal to replace public broadcasting licence fees with direct state funding, Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Bára Stárek, Executive Director of Díky, že můžem. Stárek warns that the proposed changes offer "no real safeguards" against political influence, pointing to developments in Slovakia and Hungary. She also drew a parallel with the Velvet Revolution of 1989, recalling that "we didn't have a free media and we only had a state media" under communist rule. "Media is the first (line of) attack when you want to attack democracy," she said. With the legislation expected to reach Parliament in January, Stárek believes the demonstrations will continue if the government refuses to engage in any discussions.

Сотни тысяч людей собрались в Праге в знак протеста против предложения чешского правительства заменить лицензионные сборы на общественное вещание прямым государственным финансированием, и Делано Д'Суза рад приветствовать Бару Старек, исполнительного директора Díky, že můžem. Старек предупреждает, что предлагаемые изменения не обеспечивают «реальных гарантий» от политического влияния, указывая на события в Словакии и Венгрии. Она также провела параллель с Бархатной революцией 1989 года, напомнив, что «у нас не было свободных средств массовой информации, и у нас были только государственные средства массовой информации» при коммунистическом правлении. «Медиа — это первая линия атаки, когда вы хотите атаковать демократию», — сказала она. Ожидается, что в январе этого года законопроект дойдет до парламента, и Старек считает, что демонстрации продолжатся, если правительство откажется участвовать в каких-либо дискуссиях.

Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Grégoire Roos, Director of the Europe and Russia and Eurasia Programmes at Chatham House. As European countries prepare to take part in the next round of Ukraine peace talks, Roos questions whether having five European representatives could weaken their negotiating position. "The other option is to realize that it dilutes the negotiating power of Europe. And I would lean towards that," he says, proposing Finnish President Alexander Stubb as a possible representative. Roos also points to differences between Washington and European governments over negotiations with Russia. While "the Americans do absolutely want to have a deal whatever the cost for both Ukraine and Europe," he argues that European governments have little choice but to maintain pressure on Moscow, which has yet to abandon its "maximalist demands."

articles.originalTitle: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs protest in Prague over public media funding plan
articles.originalText: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday against government plans to replace public media fees with direct state funding, which critics say threatens broadcasters’ independence. Organisers said turnout exceeded a March protest of more than 200,000, potentially making it the largest demonstration since the 1989 Velvet Revolution.
articles.originalFullText:
Hundreds of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday against government plans to replace public media fees with direct state funding, which critics say threatens broadcasters’ independence. Organisers said turnout exceeded a March protest of more than 200,000, potentially making it the largest demonstration since the 1989 Velvet Revolution.

Hundreds of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday against a government plan to cut a public media fee and move funding to the state budget — a policy critics say would dent the broadcasters' independence and viability.

Organisers said Sunday's turnout exceeded an anti-government protest of more than 200,000 people in March and predicted it could end up as the largest demonstration since the Velvet Revolution in 1989 that swept away Communist rule and propelled dissident playwright Vaclav Havel to power.

Critics have compared the government's media bill to changes in Hungary under former Prime Minister Viktor Orban, who built an array of pro-government media.

Opposition parties and civic groups also slammed the government for rushing through the initial bill in the middle of the night in October, calling for the ruling coalition to rescind the law.

"An elected government has the right to govern but it does not have the right to do whatever it wants and to dismantle democratic institutions," said Mikulas Minar, chairman of the civic group Milion Chvilek (A Million Moments) that organised Sunday's protest and estimated some 400,000 attended.

"Show that your aim is not to take control of them and let experts propose genuine safeguards for their independence from political power."

Read moreCzech author Ondracka: Velvet Revolution an ‘uprising of people who said enough’

Government accuses media of bias

The populist government of billionaire Prime Minister Andrej Babis, backed by the far-right SPD and the eurosceptic Motorists parties, accuses Czech private and public media of bias.

Its draft bill would cancel a 205-crown ($9.26) monthly household broadcasting fee currently used for funding. The bill has passed a preliminary vote and awaits further debate.

Protesters, carrying signs that read "Hands off the media" and "Let media deal with politicians", clogged nearby metro stations and filled Letna park overlooking the Czech capital. Speakers included students, soldiers and former dissidents who signed the Charter 77 initiative.

Many at the protest, staged days before a public holiday on November 17 that commemorates the start of the Velvet Revolution, wore pointed hats folded out of newspapers as a tribute to an animated character who has introduced Czech Television's nightly children's bedtime stories for decades.

"I know that our entire Czech Television is a guarantee of truth and objectivity," pensioner Milana Rudolfova, 72, told Reuters. "If we do not have public television and radio then unfortunately we will not be able to believe anything anymore."

Earlier this month, Czech public television and radio workers escalated the fight with a one-day strike that led to broadcast curbs and protests backed by artists and students.

Critics say shifting funding to the state budget would undercut the media's relationship with paying viewers and make the sector susceptible to political pressure.

A 15% financing cut proposed as part of the change would reduce television's nominal budget to the level of 2008 and that of radio to 2005. Media say that is unworkable.

Babis says the government is merely meeting a promise to lighten the financial burden on people.

(FRANCE 24 with Reuters)
articles.fullText:
Сотни тысяч чехов собрались в Праге в воскресенье против планов правительства заменить сборы за общественные СМИ прямым государственным финансированием, что, по мнению критиков, угрожает независимости вещателей. Организаторы заявили, что явка превысила мартовский протест более чем на 200 000 человек, что потенциально делает его крупнейшей демонстрацией со времен Бархатной революции 1989 года.

Сотни тысяч чехов собрались в Праге в воскресенье против правительственного плана по сокращению платы за общественные СМИ и переводу финансирования в государственный бюджет, что, по мнению критиков, подорвет независимость и жизнеспособность вещателей.

Организаторы заявили, что явка превысила антиправительственный протест более 200 000 человек в марте и предсказали, что это может стать крупнейшей демонстрацией со времен Бархатной революции в 1989 году, которая сметла коммунистическое правление и привела к власти диссидентского драматурга Вацлава Гавела.

Критики сравнили законопроект правительства о СМИ с изменениями в Венгрии при бывшем премьер-министре Викторе Орбане, который создал ряд проправительственных СМИ.

Оппозиционные партии и гражданские группы также осудили правительство за то, что оно в середине ночи в октябре пробежалось по первоначальному законопроекту, призвав правящую коалицию отменить закон.

«Избранное правительство имеет право управлять, но оно не имеет права делать все, что хочет, и демонтировать демократические институты», - сказал Микулас Минар, председатель гражданской группы Милион Чвилек, которая организовала воскресный протест и, по оценкам, приняла участие около 400 000 человек.

Покажите, что ваша цель не в том, чтобы взять их под контроль, и пусть эксперты предложат подлинные гарантии их независимости от политической власти.

Ондрачка: Бархатная революция — «восстание людей, которые сказали достаточно»

Правительство обвиняет СМИ в предвзятости

Популистское правительство миллиардера премьер-министра Андрея Бабиша, поддерживаемое крайне правой СДПГ и евроскептическими партиями «Мотористы», обвиняет чешские частные и государственные СМИ в предвзятости.

Законопроект отменяет ежемесячную плату за вещание на 205 крон ($9,26), которая в настоящее время используется для финансирования. Законопроект прошел предварительное голосование и ожидает дальнейшего обсуждения.

Протестующие, несущие плакаты с надписями «Руки прочь от СМИ» и «Пусть СМИ разбираются с политиками», засорили близлежащие станции метро и заполнили парк Летна с видом на чешскую столицу. Среди выступавших были студенты, солдаты и бывшие диссиденты, подписавшие инициативу «Хартия 77».

Многие на протесте, устроенном за несколько дней до публичного праздника 17 ноября, который ознаменовал начало Бархатной революции, носили остроконечные шляпы, сложенные из газет, как дань анимационному персонажу, который десятилетиями представлял ночные детские истории чешского телевидения.

"Я знаю, что все наше чешское телевидение - это гарантия правды и объективности", - сказала 72-летняя пенсионерка Милана Рудольфова. Если у нас не будет общественного телевидения и радио, то, к сожалению, мы не сможем больше ни во что верить.

Ранее в этом месяце чешские работники общественного телевидения и радио обострили борьбу однодневной забастовкой, которая привела к запретам на вещание и протестам, поддерживаемым художниками и студентами.

Критики говорят, что перевод финансирования в государственный бюджет подорвет отношения СМИ с платящими зрителями и сделает сектор восприимчивым к политическому давлению.

Сокращение финансирования на 15%, предложенное в рамках изменения, приведет к сокращению номинального бюджета телевидения до уровня 2008 года и радио до 2005 года. СМИ говорят, что это не работает.

Бабиш говорит, что правительство просто выполняет обещание облегчить финансовое бремя для людей.

(Франция 24 с Рейтер)
